items.title: Refactor System Templates to Use Layout Containers
items.description: Refactor all 11 system templates (Classic Light, Classic Dark, Vercel Minimal, Vercel Professional, Vercel Executive, Vercel Modern, Vercel Classic, Dark Noir, Midnight Blue, Carbon Terminal, Obsidian Elegance) from absolute positioning to use layout_container elements with column/row layouts. The visual design must remain identical - only the underlying structure changes to use the container-based layout system.
acceptance_criteria: All 11 system templates use layout_container elements instead of absolute positioning
Column containers are used for vertically stacked sections (header, billing info, tables, footer)
Row containers are used for side-by-side elements (Title+From, BillTo+Dates, Notes+Summary)
Child elements use positionMode: 'relative' with parentId references
Visual output is pixel-perfect identical to original templates
PDF export produces identical output
Table visibility toggles work correctly (work hours show/hide)
Empty containers collapse properly when showWhenEmpty: false
All token interpolation ({{invoice_number}}, etc.) works correctly
Style editor displays containers correctly
steps_to_verify: Generate PDF screenshots of all templates BEFORE refactoring
Refactor Classic Light template first as reference implementation
Compare visual output - must be identical
Refactor remaining 10 templates using same pattern
Test each template: PDF export, visibility toggles, token interpolation
Verify style editor shows containers with proper hierarchy
Screenshot comparison: BEFORE vs AFTER must match

items.description: The container-based template refactor (STYLE-001) introduced rendering issues where elements stack/overlap instead of displaying correctly. Instead of fixing the broken templates, restore the original 11 working templates (absolute positioning) and keep the new container-based templates as separate 'V2' variants for future iteration.

items.title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) System
items.description: Implement a proper RBAC system with a separate roles table containing predefined roles (user, admin) with embedded permissions. Users reference roles via foreign key. Permissions follow action:resource naming convention (e.g., read:invoices, admin:users). System is extensible for future roles without schema changes.
acceptance_criteria: roles table created with: name (unique slug), displayName, description, permissions array, isSystemRole, isDefault, sortOrder, timestamps
roles table indexes: by_name, by_default, by_system_role, by_sort_order
Permission naming convention: action:resource (e.g., read:invoices, write:invoices, admin:users, admin:system)
PERMISSIONS constant object defines all available permissions with type safety
users table has roleId field (foreign key to roles table)
users table has by_role_id index for efficient role queries
Seeded 'user' role with permissions: read/write/delete:invoices, read/write:templates, read/write:clients, read/write:profile
Seeded 'admin' role with all user permissions plus: admin:users, admin:roles, admin:templates, admin:system
'user' role marked as isDefault: true for new user assignment
Both seeded roles marked as isSystemRole: true to prevent deletion
seedAllRoles mutation is idempotent (can run multiple times safely)
getUserRoleDoc(ctx, userId) returns user's role document with permissions
hasPermission(ctx, userId, permission) checks if user has specific permission
currentUserHasPermission(ctx, permission) checks current authenticated user
requirePermission(ctx, permission) throws if user lacks permission
isAdmin(ctx) returns true if user has any admin:* permission
requireAdmin(ctx) throws if user is not admin (uses admin:system permission)
ADMIN_EMAILS env var assigns admin role instead of user role on creation
listRoles query returns all roles (admin only)
getDefaultRole query returns the role marked as isDefault
getRoleByName query returns role by name slug
useUserRole hook returns { user, role, permissions, isAdmin, hasPermission, isLoading }
AdminGuard component redirects users without admin:system permission
Admin layout wraps /admin/* routes with AdminGuard
Admin link (shield icon) visible in header only for users with admin permissions

items.title: Migrate from Legacy role Column to roleId RBAC System
items.description: Remove the legacy 'role' string column from the users table and fully adopt the roleId foreign key RBAC system. Currently both systems run in parallel - new users get both 'role' and 'roleId' set, and fallback logic reads from 'role' when 'roleId' is missing. This creates confusion and potential inconsistencies. Migrate all existing users to use roleId exclusively and remove all legacy role field references.

items.title: Fix Catch-22 Bug in seedAllRoles Admin Check
items.description: The seedAllRoles mutation has a catch-22 bug: it requires admin permission to update roles, but if admin permissions are broken (missing admin:system), no one can run it to fix them. This creates a deadlock where admins with broken permissions cannot fix their own permissions. The mutation should also accept legacy role='admin' field as fallback authentication.
acceptance_criteria: seedAllRoles checks for admin permission using BOTH roleId-based permissions AND legacy role field

promoteToAdminByEmail also sets roleId, not just role field
Admin check uses extractClerkId helper function for consistency
